/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

It is easy to see that the set of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which
quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of
quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

Here a *quasivariety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of
quasi-identities $\forall \bar x\ (w_1(\bar x) = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_n(\bar x) = 1
\Rightarrow w(\bar x) = 1)$, where $w_1, \dots, w_n, w$ are group words. A *non-trivial
identity* holds in a class $\mathfrak{K}$ if there is a group word $w \neq 1$ with
$w(\bar x) = 1$ for all $\bar x$ in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$. The *multiplication* is
the Mal'cev product: a group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{K} \cdot \mathfrak{L}$ if and only if $G$
has a normal subgroup $N \in \mathfrak{K}$ with $G / N \in \mathfrak{L}$.

Classes of groups are modelled as predicates on the groups with carrier in `Type`, so that
the quasivarieties form a set. Nothing is lost: a quasivariety is determined by its countable
members, and the Mal'cev product only involves subgroups and quotients.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables `x₀, x₁, x₂, …`:
finitely many premises `wᵢ = 1` and one conclusion `w = 1`, where the `wᵢ` and `w` are

blocks.name: QuasiIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables `x₀, x₁, x₂, …`:
finitely many premises `wᵢ = 1` and one conclusion `w = 1`, where the `wᵢ` and `w` are
group words, i.e. elements of the free group on `ℕ`. (In a group every equation `u = v`
between words is equivalent to `u * v⁻¹ = 1`, so no generality is lost.) Identities are the
quasi-identities without premises. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `wᵢ` of the premises `wᵢ = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

blocks.docstring:
The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `G`: for every assignment `x` of the
variables in `G` under which all premises evaluate to `1`, the conclusion evaluates to
`1` as well.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Sentence`/`Structure.Realize` (no group language in Mathlib), `FreeGroup.lift` (used for evaluation).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.55».QuasiIdentity / QuasiIdentity.Holds
justification.why_needed: Quasi-identities of groups (finite premises wᵢ = 1, conclusion w = 1, words in FreeGroup ℕ, evaluated via `FreeGroup.lift`) and their satisfaction in a group. Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language` has no language of groups and no notion of quasi-identity.

blocks.name: QuasiIdentity.Holds
blocks.text:
/-- The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `G`: for every assignment `x` of the
variables in `G` under which all premises evaluate to `1`, the conclusion evaluates to
`1` as well. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion = 1

blocks.code:
def IsQuasivariety (𝒦 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, q.Holds G
blocks.docstring:
A class of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups in which every
quasi-identity from some set `Q` of quasi-identities holds.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.55».IsQuasivariety
justification.why_needed: A class of groups is a quasivariety iff it is the class of models of some set of quasi-identities; not in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

blocks.name: IsQuasivariety
blocks.text:
/-- A class of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups in which every
quasi-identity from some set `Q` of quasi-identities holds. -/
def IsQuasivariety (𝒦 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, q.Holds G

blocks.docstring:
A non-trivial identity holds in the class `𝒦`: there is a group word `w ≠ 1` such
that `w(x) = 1` for every assignment `x` of the variables in every group of `𝒦`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No notion of group laws/identities in Mathlib; `FreeGroup` used for words.
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.55».HasNontrivialIdentity
justification.why_needed: Expresses 'a non-trivial identity holds in the quasivariety' (∃ w ≠ 1 in FreeGroup ℕ with w ≡ 1 on all members).

blocks.name: HasNontrivialIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A non-trivial identity holds in the class `𝒦`: there is a group word `w ≠ 1` such
that `w(x) = 1` for every assignment `x` of the variables in every group of `𝒦`. -/
def HasNontrivialIdentity (𝒦 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : FreeGroup ℕ, w ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → ∀ x : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1

blocks.code:
def malcevProduct (𝒦 𝓛 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), 𝒦 N ∧ 𝓛 (G ⧸ N)
blocks.docstring:
The (Mal'cev) product of two classes of groups: `G ∈ 𝒦 * 𝓛` if and only if `G` has a
normal subgroup `N ∈ 𝒦` with `G ⧸ N ∈ 𝓛`.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.55».malcevProduct (+ `Mul GroupClass` instance)
justification.why_needed: The multiplication of (quasi)varieties: G ∈ 𝒦·𝓛 iff G has a normal subgroup N ∈ 𝒦 with G/N ∈ 𝓛.

blocks.name: malcevProduct
blocks.text:
/-- The (Mal'cev) product of two classes of groups: `G ∈ 𝒦 * 𝓛` if and only if `G` has a
normal subgroup `N ∈ 𝒦` with `G ⧸ N ∈ 𝓛`. -/
def malcevProduct (𝒦 𝓛 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), 𝒦 N ∧ 𝓛 (G ⧸ N)

blocks.code:
def quasivarietiesWithIdentity : Set GroupClass :=
  {𝒦 | IsQuasivariety 𝒦 ∧ HasNontrivialIdentity 𝒦}
blocks.docstring: The set of all quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial identity holds.

justification.name: Kourovka.«8.55».quasivarietiesWithIdentity
justification.why_needed: The set S of the problem: quasivarieties in each of which a non-trivial identity holds.

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem trivialClass_mem_quasivarietiesWithIdentity :
    trivialClass ∈ quasivarietiesWithIdentity := by
  refine ⟨⟨{⟨∅, FreeGroup.of 0⟩}, fun G _ => ?_⟩, FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of_ne_one 0,
    fun G _ h x => ?_⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, QuasiIdentity.Holds, Finset.notMem_empty,
      IsEmpty.forall_iff, implies_true, forall_const, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of]
    exact ⟨fun h x => @Subsingleton.elim G h _ _,
      fun h => ⟨fun a b => (h fun _ => a).trans (h fun _ => b).symm⟩⟩
  · exact @Subsingleton.elim G h _ _
blocks.docstring:
The trivial quasivariety is a quasivariety (defined by the identity `x₀ = 1`) in which a
non-trivial identity holds.

blocks.docstring:
It is easy to see that the set $S$ of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which
quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of
quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

Here $S$ is `quasivarietiesWithIdentity` and the multiplication is the Mal'cev product `*`.
The trivial quasivariety $\mathfrak{E}$ lies in $S$ and is a two-sided identity element, so a
free semigroup has to be understood as in the Neumann–Šmel'kin theorem on varieties of groups:
the question is whether $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$ is a free semigroup, i.e. whether there
is a bijection $e$ from the free semigroup on some set onto $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$
with $e(xy) = e(x) \cdot e(y)$. Equivalently, $S$ is a free monoid. The multiplicativity of
$e$ includes the closure of $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$ under the product.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (Prop: the semigroup of group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial identity, under Mal'cev product — G in K·L iff G has a normal subgroup N ∈ K with G/N ∈ L — is a free semigroup); subtleties: the preamble 'it is easy to see that ... is a semigroup' is an asserted premise (closure under product uses the non-trivial-identity hypothesis), not a question; 'quasivariety in which a non-trivial identity holds' means a group quasivariety contained in some proper variety; 'free' must be read as free semigroup on some generating set (free semigroup vs. free monoid matters since the trivial quasivariety is a two-sided identity), and 'set of all quasivarieties' is a proper class-sized collection that must be modelled as a set of classes/types with a fixed universe.
claims.reviewer_why: c04's declaration (edited: fixed universe `Type` instead of universe polymorphism, line wrapping, tightened docstrings) states the only non-degenerate reading of the question: the set S of group quasivarieties satisfying a non-trivial law, minus the trivial quasivariety 𝔈, is (closed under and) isomorphic via a multiplicative bijection to `FreeSemigroup ι` for some ι — equivalently S is a free monoid. Definitions checked: quasivariety = model class of a set of quasi-identities (Finset of premise words, conclusion word in FreeGroup ℕ); non-trivial identity = word w ≠ 1 that is a law in every member; Mal'cev product G ∈ K·L iff ∃ N ⊴ G, N ∈ K, G/N ∈ L (verified with #print that the quotient group instance comes from the N.Normal witness). answer(True)/answer(False) correspond to free/not free; empty ι gives no degenerate truth. c05, c06, c07 are equivalent faithful alternatives (free-monoid or MulHom-with-range formulations). c01, c02, c03, c08 were rejected: they demand a free-semigroup isomorphism onto all of S including 𝔈, which is a two-sided identity, so their statement is trivially false (c01/c08 also quantify over all operations satisfying the Mal'cev spec, making the statement vacuous if closure failed).

decomposition_objections.text: The table says 'free' must be read as 'free semigroup on some generating set'. Read literally on the set S itself this is trivially false and hence cannot be the open question: the trivial quasivariety 𝔈 (trivial groups; defined by the identity x = 1, which is a non-trivial identity) belongs to S and is a two-sided identity element (𝔈·𝒦 = 𝒦·𝔈 = 𝒦), while a free semigroup has no identity element. The only non-degenerate reading — and the one matching the Neumann–Neumann–Neumann/Shmel'kin theorem for varieties ('the varieties other than 𝔈 and 𝔒 form a free semigroup') — is that S∖{𝔈} is a free semigroup, equivalently that S is a free monoid. I formalized this reading (as a free semigroup on S∖{𝔈}, staying as close as possible to the table's wording). Minor note: the non-trivial-identity hypothesis is what excludes the quasivariety 𝔒 of all groups, a zero element (𝔒·𝒦 = 𝒦·𝔒 = 𝔒), which would also destroy freeness; the Mal'cev product of two group quasivarieties is always a quasivariety, so the hypothesis is not needed for that.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.55

by A. Yu. Olshanskii

It is easy to see that the set of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which
quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of
quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

Here a *quasivariety* of groups is the class of all groups satisfying some set of
quasi-identities $\forall \bar x\ (w_1(\bar x) = 1 \wedge \dots \wedge w_n(\bar x) = 1
\Rightarrow w(\bar x) = 1)$, where $w_1, \dots, w_n, w$ are group words. A *non-trivial
identity* holds in a class $\mathfrak{K}$ if there is a group word $w \neq 1$ with
$w(\bar x) = 1$ for all $\bar x$ in every group of $\mathfrak{K}$. The *multiplication* is
the Mal'cev product: a group $G$ lies in $\mathfrak{K} \cdot \mathfrak{L}$ if and only if $G$
has a normal subgroup $N \in \mathfrak{K}$ with $G / N \in \mathfrak{L}$.

Classes of groups are modelled as predicates on the groups with carrier in `Type`, so that
the quasivarieties form a set. Nothing is lost: a quasivariety is determined by its countable
members, and the Mal'cev product only involves subgroups and quotients.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.55»

/-- A class of groups, modelled as a predicate on the groups with carrier in `Type`. -/
def GroupClass : Type 1 := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- A quasi-identity in the language of groups, in the variables `x₀, x₁, x₂, …`:
finitely many premises `wᵢ = 1` and one conclusion `w = 1`, where the `wᵢ` and `w` are
group words, i.e. elements of the free group on `ℕ`. (In a group every equation `u = v`
between words is equivalent to `u * v⁻¹ = 1`, so no generality is lost.) Identities are the
quasi-identities without premises. -/
structure QuasiIdentity where
  /-- The words `wᵢ` of the premises `wᵢ = 1`. -/
  premises : Finset (FreeGroup ℕ)
  /-- The word `w` of the conclusion `w = 1`. -/
  conclusion : FreeGroup ℕ

/-- The quasi-identity `q` holds in the group `G`: for every assignment `x` of the
variables in `G` under which all premises evaluate to `1`, the conclusion evaluates to
`1` as well. -/
def QuasiIdentity.Holds (q : QuasiIdentity) (G : Type) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x : ℕ → G, (∀ w ∈ q.premises, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1) →
    FreeGroup.lift x q.conclusion = 1

/-- A class of groups is a *quasivariety* if it consists exactly of the groups in which every
quasi-identity from some set `Q` of quasi-identities holds. -/
def IsQuasivariety (𝒦 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ Q : Set QuasiIdentity, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G ↔ ∀ q ∈ Q, q.Holds G

/-- A non-trivial identity holds in the class `𝒦`: there is a group word `w ≠ 1` such
that `w(x) = 1` for every assignment `x` of the variables in every group of `𝒦`. -/
def HasNontrivialIdentity (𝒦 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ w : FreeGroup ℕ, w ≠ 1 ∧
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒦 G → ∀ x : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift x w = 1

/-- The (Mal'cev) product of two classes of groups: `G ∈ 𝒦 * 𝓛` if and only if `G` has a
normal subgroup `N ∈ 𝒦` with `G ⧸ N ∈ 𝓛`. -/
def malcevProduct (𝒦 𝓛 : GroupClass) : GroupClass :=
  fun G _ => ∃ (N : Subgroup G) (_ : N.Normal), 𝒦 N ∧ 𝓛 (G ⧸ N)

instance : Mul GroupClass := ⟨malcevProduct⟩

/-- The set of all quasivarieties of groups in each of which a non-trivial identity holds. -/
def quasivarietiesWithIdentity : Set GroupClass :=
  {𝒦 | IsQuasivariety 𝒦 ∧ HasNontrivialIdentity 𝒦}

/-- The trivial quasivariety `𝔈`, consisting of the trivial groups. It is the two-sided
identity element for the multiplication of quasivarieties. -/
def trivialClass : GroupClass := fun G _ => Subsingleton G

/-- The trivial quasivariety is a quasivariety (defined by the identity `x₀ = 1`) in which a
non-trivial identity holds. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem trivialClass_mem_quasivarietiesWithIdentity :
    trivialClass ∈ quasivarietiesWithIdentity := by
  refine ⟨⟨{⟨∅, FreeGroup.of 0⟩}, fun G _ => ?_⟩, FreeGroup.of 0, FreeGroup.of_ne_one 0,
    fun G _ h x => ?_⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, QuasiIdentity.Holds, Finset.notMem_empty,
      IsEmpty.forall_iff, implies_true, forall_const, FreeGroup.lift_apply_of]
    exact ⟨fun h x => @Subsingleton.elim G h _ _,
      fun h => ⟨fun a b => (h fun _ => a).trans (h fun _ => b).symm⟩⟩
  · exact @Subsingleton.elim G h _ _

/-- The class of all groups is a quasivariety (defined by the empty set of quasi-identities). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isQuasivariety_top : IsQuasivariety (fun _ _ => True) :=
  ⟨∅, fun _ _ => by simp⟩

/-- No non-trivial identity holds in the class of all groups (it contains the free group), so
it does not belong to the semigroup in question. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem top_notMem_quasivarietiesWithIdentity :
    (fun _ _ => True) ∉ quasivarietiesWithIdentity := by
  rintro ⟨-, w, hw, h⟩
  exact hw <| (FreeGroup.lift_of_apply w).symm.trans <| h (FreeGroup ℕ) trivial FreeGroup.of

/--
It is easy to see that the set $S$ of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which
quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of
quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?

Here $S$ is `quasivarietiesWithIdentity` and the multiplication is the Mal'cev product `*`.
The trivial quasivariety $\mathfrak{E}$ lies in $S$ and is a two-sided identity element, so a
free semigroup has to be understood as in the Neumann–Šmel'kin theorem on varieties of groups:
the question is whether $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$ is a free semigroup, i.e. whether there
is a bijection $e$ from the free semigroup on some set onto $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$
with $e(xy) = e(x) \cdot e(y)$. Equivalently, $S$ is a free monoid. The multiplicativity of
$e$ includes the closure of $S \setminus \{\mathfrak{E}\}$ under the product.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.55» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (ι : Type 1) (e : FreeSemigroup ι ≃ ↥(quasivarietiesWithIdentity \ {trivialClass})),
      ∀ x y, (e (x * y) : GroupClass) = e x * e y := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.55»

items: Classes of groups are modelled as predicates `∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop` in the fixed universe `Type` (definitions are universe-polymorphic, the theorem uses universe 0). This loses nothing: a quasivariety is determined by its finitely generated (hence countable) members, and the Mal'cev product only involves subgroups and quotients, which stay in the same universe.

Quasivariety = class of all groups satisfying some set Q of quasi-identities, where a quasi-identity is a finite set of premise words wᵢ ∈ FreeGroup ℕ and a conclusion word w, read as ∀x̄ (∧ wᵢ(x̄)=1 → w(x̄)=1). Equations u = v between words are equivalent to uv⁻¹ = 1 in groups, so this is the standard notion; by Mal'cev's theorem it coincides with the semantic definition (closure under I, S, P, ultraproducts).
'A non-trivial identity holds in 𝒦' = ∃ w ∈ FreeGroup ℕ, w ≠ 1, with w(x̄) = 1 for all x̄ in all members of 𝒦 (equivalently 𝒦 is contained in a proper variety).

Multiplication is the Mal'cev product with the table's convention: G ∈ 𝒦 * 𝓛 iff ∃ N ⊴ G with ↥N ∈ 𝒦 and G ⧸ N ∈ 𝓛. It is given as a `Mul` instance on all classes of groups (not a `Semigroup`: associativity only holds for isomorphism-closed classes such as quasivarieties); the statement only uses it on elements of S.

Freeness is expressed as the existence of a bijection e : FreeSemigroup ι ≃ ↥(S \ {𝔈}) with e(x*y) = e x * e y in the ambient type; this also encodes closure of S∖{𝔈} under the product (the notebook's asserted 'easy to see' premise), which is true, so the `answer(True)`/`answer(False)` directions correspond exactly to 'free'/'not free'. The generating set ι ranges over `Type 1` (the universe of S) so no cardinality restriction is imposed.

S∖{𝔈} free semigroup is used rather than S free monoid (mathematically equivalent since 𝔈 is the identity of S); the trivial quasivariety is `trivialClass := fun G _ => Subsingleton G`, equal (by propext/funext) to any other representation of the class of trivial groups.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: the notebook says 'is this semigroup free?' about a set that literally contains the trivial quasivariety 𝔈 (it satisfies x = 1), which is a two-sided identity for the Mal'cev product. A literal 'free semigroup' reading is therefore trivially false and cannot be the intended open question; the decomposition table's note 'free must be read as free semigroup' can only be realised non-degenerately on S∖{𝔈}, which is what the final file does (matching the Neumann–Šmel'kin phrasing for varieties). This is provably equivalent to 'S is a free monoid' (K ⊆ K·L, so K·L = 𝔈 forces K = L = 𝔈); the docstring records this. Candidates c05/c06 chose the free-monoid form and c07 the free-semigroup-on-nontrivial-members form — all equivalent to the shipped statement. The preamble ('it is easy to see ... is a semigroup') is not assumed as a hypothesis: the multiplicative bijection itself entails closure of S∖{𝔈} under the product, so if the (true) premise failed the statement would simply be false rather than vacuously true. Universe restriction to groups in `Type` is faithful since a quasivariety is determined by its countable members and the product only uses subgroups and quotients; the generator type ι ranges over `Type 1` (the universe of GroupClass) so no cardinality restriction is imposed. The file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning; intended repo path FormalConjectures/Kourovka/8_55.lean.
statement: It is easy to see that the set of all quasivarieties of groups, in each of which quasivarieties a non-trivial identity holds, is a semigroup under multiplication of quasivarieties. Is this semigroup free?
